cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: skewness of the ten-value sample 3,4,5,2,3,4,5,6,4,7
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as 0.359543. Independently derived from the documented formula n/((n-1)(n-2)) * SUM(((x-mean)/s)^3) with n = 10, mean 4.3 and sample standard deviation s = 1.4181 -> 0.35954307

cases.description: A perfectly symmetric sample has zero skewness
cases.expected_note: The cubed standardized deviations of a symmetric set cancel exactly in pairs, so the sum and therefore the skewness is 0

cases.description: A single large outlier pulls the skewness positive
cases.expected_note: Derived from the documented formula: mean 3, s = 4, standardized deviations -0.5, -0.5, -0.5, 1.5; sum of cubes = 3.0; n/((n-1)(n-2)) = 4/6 = 0.66667; 0.66667*3 = 2 exactly

cases.description: The n/((n-1)(n-2)) factor is undefined below three data points
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #DIV/0! if there are fewer than three data points, because (n-2) is zero

cases.description: Identical values give a zero sample standard deviation, which cannot be divided by
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #DIV/0! if the sample standard deviation is zero, since the formula standardizes each deviation by s
